updates.summary: Economic and energy stress remained severe while the coercive apparatus showed no evidence of systemic fracture.
Diplomacy suffered a setback while fiscal and energy stress worsened; managed oil transit through Hormuz improved for Gulf producers without restoring Iran's own export position.

Monetary / FX.text: Rial remains very weak; liquidity growth and the managed/free-market spread keep medium-term crisis risk elevated.

Fiscal.text: Weak sovereign financing demand and high yields add to pressure from lost oil revenue.

Banking / payments.text: Alternative payment rails remain under sanctions pressure.

Food / medicine.text: Medicine shortages and imported-input constraints remain severe.

Energy / industrial.text: Remote work and transport conservation are implemented; the gasoline deficit persists.

Social / protest.text: Economic protests broadened but remain fragmented.

Coercive apparatus.text: No corroborated systemic pay failure, refusal, desertion or defection.

Elite cohesion.text: No high-level institutional split is visible.

External support.text: China and Russia cushion isolation but do not replace lost oil FX.

news.title: Tehran's initial Hormuz proposal was rejected
news.impact: Reduced the negotiated-de-escalation scenario and raised prolonged-standoff and escalation cases.

news.title: Managed crude flows through Hormuz increased
news.impact: Lowered physical-delivery risk slightly, but flows principally benefited Saudi and Iraqi exports rather than restoring Iranian oil revenue.

news.title: Emergency demand-management measures took effect
news.impact: Remote work, public-transport incentives and fuel-conservation measures strengthened evidence of a binding domestic energy imbalance.
